data.title: Oil Prices Mixed Ahead of OPEC+ Meeting as Middle East Supply Risks Persist — Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices were mixed on Friday as traders weighed renewed threats to Middle Eastern supplies ahead of a meeting of OPEC and its allies during the weekend.

Brent crude futures were broadly flat at $96.56 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate rose 1.8% to $85.15 a barrel. Both benchmarks pared earlier gains, having traded at $97.15 and $85.96 a barrel, respectively.

The two indicators are on track for their first weekly gain this month as geopolitical risks in the Middle East intensify, analysts at MUFG said in a note Friday.

The premium on front-month Brent futures over the following month's contract has widened to $4.28 a barrel from around $2.50 at the start of the week, the analysts said. The impact of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on oil prices is likely to be tempered by the outlook for the regional conflict, they added.

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said Thursday that an attack on the Jazan oil refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations. Authorities were assessing the damage and checking the safety of the facilities, the ministry said.

Meanwhile, an Iranian drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians, The Wall Street Journal reported. Iran denied responsibility for the attack, which comes as negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain deadlocked despite a ceasefire.

Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain at just 31% of prewar levels, according to preliminary data from Kpler. While Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong, delays to some November and December cargoes have raised concerns over the reliability of near-term Middle Eastern supplies, Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider, said.

The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and other producers in the broader group called OPEC+ are expected to discuss their collective output policy for 2027 on Sunday, with existing production agreements set to expire at the end of this year.

The group's assessment of members' sustainable production capacities will help determine individual output quotas for next year. However, disruptions to production and exports during the Iran war have complicated efforts to establish how much individual countries can pump.

It remains unclear whether Saudi Arabia--the cartel's de-facto leader--and other members will restore more supply, maintain current restrictions or consider fresh cuts to support prices.

Sunday's meeting could end without a final decision, leaving current production quotas in place for the time being, Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht said. With the exception of Iraq, most OPEC+ members are producing well below their existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to increase output further, she said.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com

data.title: IOCL faces Karnataka notice after inspection finds excess ethanol delivery, short supply of petrol
data.description:
The Karnataka government has issued a show-cause notice to IOCL over discrepancies in the measurement of ethanol and motor gasoline at its Devanagonthi terminal near Bengaluru, with inspections by the Legal Metrology Department detecting a breach in permissible proportions.

Inspection detects excess ethanol, short delivery of petrol

The inspection, conducted on November 25 using a verified master proving measure, found excess delivery of 14 litres of ethanol for every 3,000 litres measured in one of the mass flow meters, while motor gasoline was short-delivered by four to six litres for the same quantity, according to the government notice.

Another ethanol mass flow meter was found to be delivering three litres in excess for every 3,000 litres measured, the notice said.

“After the Karnataka Government exposed over-blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed E20 limit, our Legal Metrology Department has begun inspecting Oil Marketing Company (OMC) terminals, where the blending is carried out,” Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad said in a Facebook post on Friday.

The minister said the inspection findings were beyond permissible limits and that a show-cause notice has been issued under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.

IOCL asked to explain discrepancies within seven days

In its notice to the Deputy General Manager and terminal in-charge of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Devanagonthi facility, the department sought an explanation for the discrepancies, details of the latest calibration and maintenance of the measuring equipment, and corrective measures to ensure compliance with the law.

The company has been directed to submit its written explanation, along with verification certificates, calibration and maintenance records, within seven days of receiving the notice.

It has also been directed not to use the concerned measuring systems for further commercial transactions until their accuracy and compliance with statutory requirements are established. Failure to submit a satisfactory explanation could invite further legal and departmental action, the notice said.

Action follows Karnataka’s E20 petrol blending allegations

The latest action comes amid a row involving the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies over alleged blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed 20 per cent limit.

On November 6, Arshad alleged that petrol supplied by major OMCs contained ethanol beyond the prescribed E20 limit. Tests on samples collected from seven districts recorded levels as high as 31.2 per cent in IOCL petrol and 30.5 per cent in HPCL petrol.

The same day, IOCL, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), in a joint statement, rejected the allegations, saying the findings were not based on testing conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedures.

They maintained that the E20 petrol supplied by them conformed to the Bureau of Indian Standards specification IS 17021.

On November 9, Arshad reiterated that the state government stood by its findings and challenged the OMCs to explain the ethanol content in 63 samples collected from petrol pumps across Karnataka.

data.title: Dollar set for flat week, still close to 22-month peak
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar unchanged after Thanksgiving, set for modest weekly rise
  • Risk-sensitive currencies rise with US stock futures
  • Dollar garners support from higher US yields, safe-haven demand

By Stefano Rebaudo

The dollar was still close to its highest level in 22 months after a the tech rout drove investors towards safe-haven assets.

The dollar index started its rally in early November and hit a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier this week. It was last little changed at 103.80 and on track for a modest weekly rise of about 0.03%.

US stock futures rose on Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares, following a seesawing of AI stocks this week as investors weighed more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology.

"We expect the Fed to remain hawkish and the US economy resilient, and our multi-asset strategists remain upbeat on US equities and the AI theme," said Daragh Maher, senior forex strategist at HSBC.

"The main risk to our view is that renewed market weakness could erode rate support, with no guarantee that safe-haven demand would again compensate," he said, adding that December’s Fed rate forecasts would be pivotal to the bullish cyclical greenback story.

If the tech rout fades, investors may strengthen expectations of Federal Reserve tightening, boosting Treasury yields and the dollar's yield appeal, even as improving risk sentiment curbs demand for the currency as a safe haven.

However investors remained cautious despite Friday's sharp rise in US stock futures.

"The high-beta Australian dollar, Kiwi dollar and Norwegian krone are leading gains in G10, although the moves remain modest compared with their recent losses," Francesco Pesole, forex strategist at ING, said.

"That suggests the forward-looking forex market remains cautious about calling an all-clear on risk sentiment," he added.

A so-called high-beta currency tends to amplify shifts in global sentiment, outperforming when risk appetite improves and underperforming when it fades.

The Norwegian crown rose 0.25% to 9.74 versus the greenback.

The Aussie dollar added 0.70% to $0.667, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

The New Zealand dollar was also supported by results of the general election, which reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner.

Geopolitics remained in the background but oil prices were on track to snap a three-week losing streak following attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure.

Higher Brent crude futures often underpin the dollar against the euro and yen, as they boost revenues for US energy exporters while increasing import costs for the euro zone and Japan.

The euro was roughly unchanged at $1.0964 with investors showing little reaction to news that Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos was set to be nominated as the head of the European Central Bank.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"The yen is understandably weaker today given the strong rebound in risk that has helped lift US Treasury bond yields," Derek Halpenny, strategist at MUFG, said.

"Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9."

Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields rose 5 bps to 4.90%.

data.title: Polish president vetoes changes to tax system
data.description:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki vetoed a change to Poland's income tax system on Friday, rejecting a bill that would have raised the personal tax threshold for around 3.5 million taxpayers but also increased corporate tax for the largest companies.

The bill would have raised the first personal tax threshold to 130,000 zlotys ($32,000) from 120,000, introduced a new 24% rate for income between 130,000 and 150,000 zlotys, and also raised the solidarity levy and corporate tax for large firms to 22% from 19%.

In a video posted on social media, Nawrocki said the reform was being sold as relief for the middle class but in fact left out roughly nine in 10 taxpayers.

"The reform primarily benefits the highest earners," he said. "Public sector workers and those earning around the median – that is, approximately 7,500 zlotys gross – were excluded."

He also objected to raising corporate tax for companies with revenue topping 50 million euros ($55 million), saying the increase would push up consumer prices, squeeze wage growth and slow investment.

"The President has once again sided with the big corporations rather than with the Polish people," Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski said in a post on X.

data.title: S&P downgrades Tata Motors PV on JLRs weak performance
data.description:
S&P Global Ratings downgraded Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and its wholly owned subsidiaries, citing Jaguar Land Rover's weaker-than-expected operating performance and negative free cash flow.

The rating agency said it lowered the long-term credit rating on Tata Motors PV and subsidiary TML Holdings Pte Ltd to BBB-' with a stable outlook from 'BBB' with a negative outlook. The rating on JLR has been lowered to BB+' with a stable outlook from BBB- with a negative outlook.

Weak profitability and negative free operating cash flow (FOCF) at Jaguar Land Rover Automotive PLC will likely delay financial recovery at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd, S&P said.

JLR's weak profitability is expected to continue to be a drag on Tata Motors PV earnings. The British luxury brand accounts for about 80 per cent of Tata Motors PV's consolidated revenue.

S&P estimates Tata Motors PV's adjusted EBITDA margin to improve to only about 0.4 per cent in the financial year 2027 from 0.2 per cent in the previous year.

S&P said JLR will struggle with weak sales volume and market conditions, as sales of imported vehicles in China fell 35 per cent year on year in the first half of the financial year 2027.

This will weaken JLR's recovery prospects this year, the rating agency said, adding that it now expects JLR's free cash flow to turn positive in the financial year 2028, rather than in this financial year.

For the second quarter ended September, Tata Motors PV reported a consolidated loss of ₹5,531 crore, compared with a profit of ₹76,170 crore in the year-ago period.

JLR recorded exceptional items of 530 million pounds in the quarter, reflecting restructuring activities, including separation costs and the write-down of intangible assets under development.

JLR has also lowered its revenue and margin guidance for the current financial year, citing geopolitical risks and costs related to restructuring. Full-year revenue is now projected at 25 billion pounds, while pre-tax margin is seen at 2-3 per cent.

S&P estimates JLR's annual capex and R&D spending in the range of 3.3-3.4 billion pounds over this and the next financial years as the brand is undertaking a major portfolio refresh.

This results in S&P Global Ratings-adjusted FOCF of about negative 1.4 billion pounds for JLR in fiscal 2027, the rating agency said.

However, with higher sales volume, JLR's plan to save 1.7 billion pounds in costs and reduce its cash flow break-even level to 300,000 wholesale units annually, S&P expects a turnaround to positive FOCF in the next financial year.

"As a result, we expect Tata Motors PV's FOCF to be marginally positive in fiscal 2028 and around Rs 140 billion in fiscal 2029, from negative Rs 152 billion in fiscal 2027", the rating agency said.

Meanwhile, Tata Motors PV's standalone sales are seen growing robustly. The company's net cash position in India, on the back of a robust operational environment, reflects the one-notch difference in S&P's rating on it from that on JLR.

While constituting about 20 per cent of consolidated revenue, we believe Tata Motors PV's stand-alone operations will generate healthy operating cash flow sufficient to fund a large part of its planned capex on capacity expansion and new model launches, the agency said.

data.title: Brazil’s stock exchange pushes stablecoin launch back to 2027
data.description:
Brazil’s stock exchange B3 is moving ahead with 2027 plans for a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, after initially targeting a launch this year.

B3 is collaborating with six of Brazil’s largest financial institutions, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP, to launch the stablecoin in the first quarter of 2027, according to a Friday report by local news outlet Valor Econômico.

Called Open BRL, the stablecoin is to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one Brazilian real. B3 will operate the underlying technology.

The initiative marks a new stage in the exchange’s digital asset strategy as Brazil’s financial industry prepares to bring traditional securities onto blockchain networks.

B3’s stablecoin plans stretch into 2027

B3 first disclosed plans to introduce its own stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026.

As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly still preparing to launch a stablecoin called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and integration with financial institutions scheduled for August and September.

B3RL was designed to be backed by Brazilian reais and secured by government bonds, and to facilitate blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027.

It remains unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. Cointelegraph reached out to B3 for clarification but had not received a response by publication.

Tokenized stocks face regulatory hurdles

B3 also plans to introduce trading of tokenized shares in early 2027, initially using the same order book as conventional equities.

The platform would initially retain its two-business-day settlement cycle rather than introduce instant settlement, Humberto Costa, a B3 executive overseeing digital asset products, reportedly said in October.

Costa also said B3RL would not handle settlement of tokenized shares at launch and that round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework.

Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring a new regulatory framework for tokenization, presenting the progress of its dedicated working group at an industry meeting in October.

data.title: Energiekontor faces financial reporting probe after abrupt outlook cut
data.description:
November 27 (Renewables Now) - The German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) has launched an examination of Energiekontor’s (ETR:EKT) 2025 annual and 2026 half-year financial reporting after the German wind and solar developer-operator cut its pre-tax profit expectations for the current year.

The probe was triggered after Energiekontor published its 2026 half-year report on August 13, confirming its target for an annual pretax profit of between EUR 40 million (USD 43.9m) and EUR 60 million. Later in the same day, however, the company issued an ad hoc announcement, slashing the forecast to a range of between EUR 5 million and EUR 10 million.

“The close timing of the ad hoc announcement and the interim financial statements is unusual and regrettable ” but it was triggered by the “change in the information available, which necessitated disclosure without undue delay,” the company said.

The forecast was lowered after it became clear that a legal issue, related to a UK grid operator, will delay the grid connection of three Scottish wind projects developed by Energiekontor. Consequently, the delay affected the sale processes for the projects.

BAFIN will now examine whether Energiekontor’s reporting took account of all information actually available. The regulator will also investigate whether deferred tax assets recognised in respect of tax loss carryforwards meet the requirements for probable utilisation.

Energiekontor stressed that the developments in the UK became known only after the publication of the half-year report. Furthermore, the issues result only in project delays, not cancellations. They do not necessitate write-downs or impairment losses related to the projects.

The German company has already received updated grid connection offers for the wind farms and is currently reviewing them. Discussions and due diligence processes with investors are continuing.

(EUR 1 = USD 1.097)

data.title: Brazil loan defaults hit fresh record as households struggle with debt burden
data.description:
Brazil's delinquency rate on loans to companies and households in the free-credit segment, where interest rates are set by lenders, rose to a record 6.7% in October, central bank data showed on Friday.

The measure increased 1.1 percentage points from the end of last year, highlighting the pressure on borrowers as high interest rates continue to weigh on disposable income and debt-servicing capacity.

  • Delinquency in free-credit loans to households alone rose to a record 8.2%, the highest level since the current series began in March 2011

  • Defaults continued to worsen in some of the most expensive credit lines for consumers, reaching 65.9% in revolving credit card debt, 16.1% in overdraft facilities and 16.1% in unsecured personal loans

  • Earlier this week, the central bank unveiled new measures aimed at curbing household indebtedness

  • Total household indebtedness, measured as outstanding debt relative to income accumulated over the previous 12 months, edged down to 50.0% in September from 50.1% in August, which had marked a record high, showed separate central bank data

  • Total outstanding loans in Brazil, including both free and subsidized credit, rose 0.4% in October from the previous month to 7.5 trillion reais ($1.33 trillion)

  • Annual credit growth slowed to 7.8% in October, from 8.5% in the 12 months through September, pointing to a gradual loss of momentum in lending activity

($1 = 5.6513 reais)

data.title: Argo Defence Group awarded framework agreement with the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) with a contract value of up to approximately SEK 13 million
data.description:
Argo Defence Group AB (publ), through its wholly owned subsidiary Swedish Net Air & Defence AB, has been awarded a framework agreement by the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) for heat lamps with accessories with a contract value of up to approximately SEK 13 million over a contract period of two years with an option to extend for a further two years. The agreement has not yet been entered into due to a ten-day standstill period.

The award decision concerns the procurement of heat lamps with accessories intended for warming individuals at risk of hypothermia in connection with traffic accidents, rescue operations, exposure to cold water, and other disaster and crisis situations.

“The award decision is welcome news and further strengthens our position as a supplier within defence and civil preparedness. The ability to rapidly provide warmth to individuals at risk of hypothermia is of great importance in both rescue operations and crisis situations, and we are proud to contribute to Sweden’s civil preparedness,” says Mariem Butler, CEO of Swedish Net Air & Defence.

In accordance with applicable legislation, a ten-day standstill period applies from the date on which the award decision was announced, during which the agreement may not be entered into. During the standstill period – and until the agreement is entered into – an application for judicial review of the procurement may be submitted to the competent administrative court. If such an application is submitted, an extended standstill period applies while the administrative court reviews the case, meaning that the agreement cannot be entered into until the proceedings have been concluded. Argo Defence Group will provide further information when available.

For further information, please contact:

Marcus Selme, CEO, Argo Defence Group AB (publ)

Telephone: +46 (0)70-629 85 61

E-mail: ir@argodefence.se

This information is information that Argo Defence Group is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-11-27 13:31 CET.

About Argo Defence Group AB (publ)

Argo Defence Group is a growth-oriented defence group with a focus on customers within both military and civil defence. The Company consists of six subsidiaries: Swedish Net Air & Defence, Disarmament Solutions, Disarmament Solutions Ukraine, Poseidon Diving Group, Zel-Aaren Innovation and LPG Trafikmarkeringar. Argo Defence Group operates through three business areas: Defence Materiel, Counter-Explosive Risk Solutions and Airfield Operations. Together, these business areas enable Argo Defence Group to offer a broad and complementary range of defence-related products and services that contribute to increased resilience and security across the Nordic region, Ukraine and internationally. The Company is listed on Nordic SME, a marketplace operated by Nordic Growth Market (NGM). Learn more at www.argodefence.se

data.title: Deutsche Börse Wins EU Clearance For Allfunds Acquisition
data.description:
ESCHBORN (dpa-AFX) - Deutsche Börse AG (DB1.DE) Friday said it has received unconditional approval from the European Commission for its planned €5.35 billion acquisition of Allfunds Group, clearing a key regulatory hurdle following a Phase I review.

The transaction remains subject to additional regulatory approvals and the sanction of the scheme of arrangement by the competent English court. Completion is now expected in the first quarter of 2027.

'Today we unconditionally approved Deutsche Börse's acquisition of Allfunds, which combines complementary businesses offering fund management services through platforms,' said Teresa Ribera, Executive Vice-President for Clean, Just and Competitive Transition.

On Xetra, Deutsche Börse shares rose 0.16% to €317.80 on Friday.

data.title: EU wheat extends gains on Black Sea disruption
data.description:
Euronext wheat prices climbed to one-month highs on Friday as ongoing war disruption to Black Sea trade maintained expectations of strong demand for European Union supplies.

Gains on broader financial markets as AI-related investor worries subsided also helped to underpin Euronext as participants awaited the reopening of Chicago grain markets after Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday.

March wheat , the most active position on Euronext, was up 1.5% at €241.25 ($264.89) a metric ton at 1220 GMT. The contract earlier reached €242 for its highest since October 20 and above a previous one-month peak of €239 on Wednesday.

Front-month December wheat rose 1.4% to €247.25 a ton after touching another one-month high at €248.25.

A Russian attack on two cargo ships carrying more than 100,000 tons of grain near the Ukrainian Black Sea port of Odesa this week has kept the focus on disruption to grain trade.

The strike further dampened hopes of a shipping truce in Russia's war with Ukraine and raised the prospect of more demand shifting towards European Union exporting countries.

Weather forecasts projecting a cold spell in the Black Sea zone from next week could also curb exports because icy conditions complicate logistics, traders said.

Winter conditions could also hamper Russian efforts to ship grain on alternative routes via the Baltic Sea and the Arctic.

Traders were also assessing competition from cheaply offered wheat from Argentina's harvest.

Argentina's 2026/27 wheat production forecast, currently expected at 23.4 million tons, could be raised due to higher than expected yields as the harvest progresses, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said on Thursday.

However, reports of modest protein content could make the Argentine crop less attractive to milling wheat importers, traders said.

A large tender being held by Pakistan, which is seeking to buy 800,000 tons with a bidding deadline on Monday, is being watched for a gauge of export competition.

Nearly all recently sown soft wheat in France remained in good or excellent condition as of Monday, data from farm office FranceAgriMer showed.

Frosts in northern France on Friday were not expected to pose any risks to crops, traders said.

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: Clavister Secures 450 MSEK Contract from BAE Systems for Clavister CyberArmour
data.description:
Örnsköldsvik, Sweden – 27 November 2026 – Clavister, a leader in European cybersecurity for mission-critical applications, today announces that it has been awarded a 450 MSEK contract by BAE Systems to supply Clavister CyberArmour as the secure digital backbone of CV90 vehicles in the multi-nation procurement programme commonly referred to as “Nordic Edition”.

The new agreement builds on Clavister CyberArmour’s established role in the CV90’s onboard communications infrastructure, bringing the solution to the Nordic Edition programme and expanding its scope within each vehicle to cover additional use cases and capabilities. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in 2028, with revenue to be recognised over several years. The Nordic Edition programme brings together procurement of CV90 vehicles for multiple nations. For Clavister, the contract represents a significant expansion of its established relationship with BAE Systems and provides long-term delivery visibility within its defence business.

The CV90 is a highly digitalised combat platform, integrating advanced vehicle systems and networked capabilities. These systems depend on a resilient digital infrastructure that connects onboard equipment, carries critical data and protects communications against cyber threats.

Clavister CyberArmour provides the vehicle’s Ethernet and IP networking infrastructure, connecting onboard systems and supplying power to many of the connected devices. It combines these functions with the full security capabilities of Clavister’s firewall technology, bringing networking, device power and cyber protection together in a solution designed for demanding military environments. This makes CyberArmour an integral part of how the vehicle’s digital systems operate and communicate.

John Vestberg, CEO of Clavister, commented: “This contract marks a major milestone in our collaboration with BAE Systems. CyberArmour forms the secure digital backbone of the CV90, connecting its onboard systems, powering devices and protecting critical communications. Its expanded role in the Nordic Edition programme demonstrates the trust placed in our technology as an integral part of the vehicle. It also shows how our strategy of embedding our technology into established defence platforms translates into substantial business as procurement programmes expand. We look forward to supporting BAE Systems over the coming years.”

The agreement reinforces Clavister’s position as a European provider of secure digital infrastructure for the defence industry and highlights the growing importance of integrated networking and cybersecurity in modern combat vehicles.

About Clavister

Clavister is a Swedish cybersecurity company that has protected mission-critical customers for over two decades. Headquartered in Örnsköldsvik, Sweden, Clavister pioneered one of the first firewalls and continues to deliver adaptive, high-performance cybersecurity solutions for public sector, energy, telecom and defence customers.

The stock, Clavister AB, is listed at Nasdaq First North Growth Market. FNCA Sweden AB is the Company’s Certified Advisor.

For additional information, please visit https://www.clavister.com/, and follow us on our official LinkedIn and YouTube channels.

For further information, please contact:

Clavister:

John Vestberg, President and CEO

Email: john.vestberg@clavister.com

This information is information that Clavister AB is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-11-27 13:23 CET.
